# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Casey Hayes
**Member ID:** W225149976
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-11
**Reference number:** POC-8E43F25837-44913
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 ([link](https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf))

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which was denied in the notice dated 2026-08-11, reference number POC-8E43F25837-44913. The stated reason for denial was that my documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your possession address the plan's own criteria. I am asking that this decision be reconsidered.

## Why I believe the documentation supports medical necessity

The plan's own policy states:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

and lists, among the requirements:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

Here is how my records address each part of this:

- **Groin-dominant pain and impingement testing:** My exam notes document "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and range of motion "limited by pain." I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain, and I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I cannot run or squat.
- **Failed non-surgical management:** I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-26 through 2026-07-21) focused on core and hip stabilization, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this is a course of provider-directed non-surgical management spanning well over three months, which did not resolve my symptoms.
- **Imaging:** An MRI arthrogram on 2026-06-08 showed an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, joint space preserved, Tonnis grade 0.

The policy also states:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Procedures and Conditions Not Addressed Elsewhere Indications CMM.JT.IN.314 v1.0.2026 Arthroscopic or open hip surgery is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following:"

I was not given the specific list that follows this heading in the denial notice or in the materials provided to me, so I am not able to address it point by point here. I am asking that my full chart, including the imaging report, physical therapy discharge note, and surgeon's clinical notes, be reviewed against the complete text of this section and the FAI section above.

If any specific document or data point is still considered missing, I am asking that Cigna identify exactly what is needed so that my provider's office can supply it, rather than denying the request as a whole for incomplete documentation.

## What I am asking for

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial in light of the clinical documentation already submitted, and approve the requested hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), or clearly identify any specific missing item so it can be provided promptly.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-07**. I am submitting it online at my.cigna.com, and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member card, and/or by mailing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, since that address is specific to my plan.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

Enclosures: [physical therapy discharge note], [MRI arthrogram report, 2026-06-08], [surgeon's clinical notes, Dr. Okafor], [medication/injection records]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
